publishedIdentity.status: all published receipts verify under the site-derived key

verdict.publishedIdentity: all published receipts verify under the site-derived key
verdict.reason: Message domain, not key type: openreceipts signs canonical JSON, the v0 envelope signs a legacy System transfer wire. The key itself is adoptable after a mechanical PEM->raw conversion and is the key behind the published receipts, but without a message-grant envelope the daemon would hold a key it cannot use, so no migration is built.

notes: Card note of 27.10. said "probably not, Ed25519 instead of Solana-Tx": the verdict holds, the reason does not. Both are Ed25519.
import refusing the PEM as stored is correct fail-closed behaviour, not a bug: it must not guess key encodings.

Published identity (pinned key match + every receipt verified under the site-derived key) is measured here for the first time; an earlier run only cross-checked OpenSSL against web3.js, which proves derivation but not identity.
Reproduced with test/envelope-fit.test.js, which runs offline in CI against a generated key, a pinned key, and two receipts (one the site key must verify, one it must NOT).
